Native birth-death-sampling profile-likelihood fit (BDSKY-equivalent generative model, maximum likelihood rather than Bayesian MCMC): Re=0.9961, 95% likelihood-ratio interval [0.99, 1.01]. becomeUninfectiousRate held at 73.0500/yr, the reciprocal of the supplied 5.0-day generation time; samplingProportion profiled over [0.002, 0.80] and best at 0.002; log-likelihood=-151.7247 over 137 Re grid points. delta is held rather than fitted because (Re, delta, s) has a likelihood ridge along which a free three-parameter fit returns whatever its starting point happened to be near.

Re is sensitive to the generation time: because delta = 365.25/generationTime scales the whole birth-death process, a generation time wrong by a factor of k moves Re by roughly the same factor. The 5.0-day value used here came from --generation-time-days or the bundled table; check it is right for this pathogen before quoting the number.

The discarded columns were positions where at least one sequence had no data, so every index now compares observed bases rather than absent coverage. Note this is NOT a re-alignment: the input was correctly aligned, it simply pooled sequences with different coverage windows.

Re: no --incidence data and --generation-time-days was left at its default (5 days, tuned for a fast viral epidemic) -- Re is highly sensitive to this value and a wrong generation time can silently compress a real growth-rate difference toward Re=1, reading as false stability. Set --generation-time-days to a value appropriate for this pathogen's actual transmission cycle (e.g. much longer for a vector-borne parasite with a multi-week tick/vector cycle than for a directly-transmitted respiratory virus) before trusting this Re.

--trim-to-covered: remapped 1 gene annotation(s) onto the trimmed coordinates. Gene spans supplied against the untrimmed alignment would otherwise fall outside it and be skipped, silently costing the dN/dS and CAI the trim was meant to recover.

CAI: no --codon-usage supplied; using the bundled 'sheep' reference table (real data from the Kazusa Codon Usage Database, not this dataset's own host) -- supply --codon-usage for a genuine dataset-specific host reference instead.

GC_Deviation: no --reference-gc supplied; using the alignment's own reference sequence's GC% (26.84%, from 'PV577423.1') as the baseline instead -- deviation is measured from THIS dataset's reference, not an external host-genome target; supply --reference-gc explicitly for that.

GC_Deviation: organism-class is 'virus', so a large GC deviation is NOT reported as horizontal gene transfer. Classical HGT (conjugation, transformation, transduction) is a documented mechanism in bacteria, but is not how viruses or eukaryotic parasites typically acquire compositional shifts -- for those, mutational pressure (e.g. APOBEC/ADAR editing) or host-driven composition bias is the usual explanation. The deviation value itself is unchanged; only its interpretation is.
